transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Ramos (Northpoint CTO), Priya Singh (Northpoint Senior ML Eng), Jordan Lee (Northpoint Platform Eng)

Auto-generated summary: quick SDK walkthrough, auth discussion, next steps to provision trial and run benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me all right?
[00:05] Alex Ramos: yep, loud and clear, maya thanks for setting this up. we got Priya and Jordan on the call as well.
[00:11] Maya Chen: great, i'll hand over to Daniel for the walkthrough but quick context: we're gonna show the python and typescript sdk quickstarts, auth patterns (api key vs sso), and a brief Console tour for keys and observability.
[00:22] Daniel Ortiz: cool, hi all. i'll start with the python quickstart, open saved link in the chat, it's the repo with a minimal example that uses environment variables for the REDWOOD_API_KEY and shows streaming and non-streaming.
[00:35] Priya Singh: perfect. one quick thing up front, we have strict KMS requirements and also want to see if private deployment (VPC) is possible for the POC.
[00:44] Maya Chen: absolutely, we support private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations — we'll share the compliance/security doc. Daniel will show the Console bits for key rotation and audit logs.
[00:53] Daniel Ortiz: ok jumping in. python example: pip install redwood-sdk (typo in repo says redwood-client in one file, sorry), then set REDWOOD_API_KEY; sample code: client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.chat.create(...). shows streaming with client.chat.stream for chunked responses.
[01:14] Jordan Lee: are there official typing hints and async support? we run asyncio for inference fan-out.
[01:20] Daniel Ortiz: yes, python has async client methods and type hints. typescript side has native promises/async await, and both SDKs handle chunked streaming and function/tool calls.
[01:32] Maya Chen: note: we sometimes call the sdk packages slightly different in docs — repo will be updated, sorry for the inconsistency.
[01:40] Daniel Ortiz: switching to typescript quickstart: npm i @redwoodai/sdk — then set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or use .env, example shows const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1-large', input: '...' })
[01:58] Priya Singh: do you have official examples for streaming and for function calling? we use function calling to integrate with our backend.
[02:06] Daniel Ortiz: yes both. the typescript example includes function calling and shows registering a function schema then handling calls. also shows how to use the Console debug logs to see function call payloads.
[02:20] Alex Ramos: on auth — we prefer SSO for user access and short-lived tokens for services. can we use SAML SSO + role-based API tokens?
[02:30] Maya Chen: Yes. Redwood Console supports SSO (SAML/SCIM) for users and we have scoped API tokens that can be short-lived. for service-to-service, you can use short-lived tokens issued by our control plane integrated with your IdP or you can rotate long-lived keys via KMS.
[02:47] Daniel Ortiz: demoing Console now, click on "API Keys" — you can create scoped keys (read-only, inference-only), set expiration, attach a policy, and enable automatic rotation. the audit logs show token creation and usage. note the audit log UI is sometimes paginated odd (small bug) — logs are there though.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: concerning data residency and private deployment: if we go private, do you still offer the Console or is it a control-plane-only option?
[03:20] Maya Chen: we offer a private control plane option. there's a customer-managed control plane for on-prem or VPC, and you can either host the Console privately or use our hosted console with a VPN link depending on the contract. we'll send the architecture diagram.
[03:36] Priya Singh: great. also, can you show environment setup—for reproducible builds we use docker images and ephemeral creds in CI.
[03:45] Daniel Ortiz: sure; recommended pattern: store REDWOOD_API_KEY in your secrets manager; for CI, inject as env var at runtime; dockerfile sets ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY placeholder; we also show a sample k8s secret manifest in the repo. note: one of the repo files references "K V cash" instead of "KV cache" — transcription/typo in doc, apologies.
[04:10] Alex Ramos: we typically do batching and want to see how Optimize suggests batching configs.
[04:16] Daniel Ortiz: Optimize will analyze your request distribution and suggest batch sizes, cache prefixing, and quantization levels. in the Console Optimize tab you'll upload a small sample or connect to tracing; it returns suggested batch sizes per model and estimated cost savings.
[04:33] Priya Singh: what's the expected latency hit if we enable quantization? for our use case 95th pct latency is critical.
[04:41] Daniel Ortiz: depends on model and profile; for many models int8 quant can add ~5-20ms per token but reduces GPU memory and cost a lot. for 95th percentile latency-critical routes we recommend dedicated capacity pinning and smaller batch windows; Optimize suggests per-route configs.
[04:58] Maya Chen: i want to call out routing/fallbacks — you can define policy to prefer hosted for dev, dedicated for prod, and fallback to a cheaper variant if a model is unavailable. this helps with graceful degradation.
[05:12] Alex Ramos: okay, on billing and cost, how do we estimate unit cost from your console/reports?
[05:19] Daniel Ortiz: Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-model and per-route metrics. there's also a cost simulator for projected spend given QPS and seq lengths. we'll share the spreadsheet template we use.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: cross-org access — do you support cross-namespace routing? we have multiple product teams.
[05:40] Maya Chen: yes, multi-namespace support with RBAC, and you can set up shared routes.
[05:46] Priya Singh: quick note — we might need PCI adjacent compliance and have strict log retention windows. what are retention options?
[05:55] Daniel Ortiz: retention is configurable per deployment; hosted defaults but enterprise/private deployments can set retention and disable payload logging. KMS integration encrypts at rest.
[06:07] Alex Ramos: good. next, can you show a quick end-to-end demo of calling the python sdk from a small flask app?
[06:14] Daniel Ortiz: yes starting screen share… (walkthrough: create virtualenv, pip install, set env var, simple endpoint that calls client.chat.create; shows streaming response to client via SSE).
[06:40] Priya Singh: small nit — the sample uses redwood-1-large model name, do you have recommended model for low-latency/low-cost?
[06:47] Daniel Ortiz: we recommend redwood-1-medium or quantized variants for cost-sensitive routes; Optimize will suggest the best match based on your dataset.
[06:56] Maya Chen: wrapping up the demo portion: we've dropped links to quickstart repos in chat, and we'll update the typos noted.
[07:04] Alex Ramos: thanks. wanted to talk about POC scope and timeline — we need to validate latency and cost for our real workload within two weeks.
[07:12] Maya Chen: that's doable. suggested POC: 2-week pilot, we provision trial dedicated namespace, you'll provide example traces and target SLOs, we'll run benchmarks and share results and config suggestions.
[07:24] Priya Singh: sounds good. also want to confirm support during pilot — SE access, runbooks?
[07:30] Maya Chen: yes you'll get SE hours included for pilot to help run benchmarks and interpret results.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: last question — can we rotate keys programmatically and have the SDK pick up new keys without restart?
[07:43] Daniel Ortiz: recommended pattern: use short-lived tokens via our token service and refresh at the client. SDK supports token provider callback so you can fetch fresh token on expiry without restart.
[07:56] Alex Ramos: perfect. any gotchas?
[07:59] Daniel Ortiz: watch for varied seq length distribution — that impacts batching behavior; also ensure your prefix cache keys are deterministic to get caching wins.
[08:12] Maya Chen: recap — action items: we send quickstarts + repos, provision trial namespace, customer to provide workload traces and SLOs, schedule benchmark session on 2025-11-18.
[08:26] Alex Ramos: thanks, that timeline works. appreciate the demos.
[08:30] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and invite for the benchmark slot.
[08:36] (meeting ends)
notes: Transcript contains a few typos and minor mislabels (e.g., 'K V cash' instead of 'KV cache') — doc team to fix repo files.
